findings.description: __aexit__ discards the real exception arguments and forwards None, None, None to __exit__, so an exception raised inside an `async with` block is recorded as a successful attempt instead of a failure.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `async with AttemptManager(retry_state) as attempt: raise ValueError()` inside an async retry loop. Mechanism: __aexit__ receives exc_type and exc_value but passes None, None, None to self.__exit__, which takes the no-exception branch and calls retry_state.set_result(None), then returns None so the exception propagates or is treated as success depending on the caller. Impact: the failed attempt is never recorded as an exception, so the retry policy does not retry, and the caller gets a silent wrong result (None) instead of the error or a retry.
